rawRequest: add seat selection to interstellar booking
objective: Travelers currently cannot select cabin seats during the interstellar booking flow, resulting in customer service overhead and a 24% drop-off at checkout.
userGoal: Select and reserve an available cabin seat before finalizing payment.
outcomes: Interactive cabin seat map renders within 300ms of booking step 2
Seat selection state is preserved and locked for 10 minutes
Selected seat number appears on booking confirmation receipt and ticket

evidence.excerpt: I was assigned a windowless lower-deck bunk without being asked. I needed an observation deck seat.
24% checkout abandonment observed on step 2 when seat assignment is automated.

constraints: Must not modify core billing or pricing calculation engines
Must preserve backwards compatibility with single-cabin cargo vessels
Cannot use third-party CDN libraries — all assets must be bundled locally

edgeCases.scenario: Two travelers select the same luxury suite simultaneously
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: First hold transaction succeeds; second traveler receives real-time seat unavailable notification and map refreshes.

edgeCases.scenario: Seat hold timer expires after 10 minutes without checkout
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Seat is returned to available pool and customer is prompted to extend or re-select.

healthMetrics: API response time p95 stays below 250ms for seat map queries
Zero regressions in existing cargo booking flow
verification: Unit test for CabinMap component rendering all 3 vessel tiers
Integration test for concurrency conflict resolution on seat hold
End-to-end checkout flow confirms seat assignment persisted in booking record
